USM Orientation Transit Operations Plan

Official Staged Transit and Hall Ingress Operational Blueprint

Executive Summary: This plan coordinates student movements for orientation day. All student hostels release at 06:00:00 (t=0). The operational bus fleet contains exactly 8 buses: 5 coach buses and 3 electric buses. Desasiswa Tekun and Desasiswa Saujana receive priority staging. Restu students wait at the Restu cafe and depart last.

1. Core Operational Directives

The transit system provides continuous loop service between hostel staging zones and Dewan Tuanku Syed Putra (DTSP). PPSL student leaders supervise headcount and queue lines. DTSP provides 3,000 full-hall seats. Dewan Budaya G03 provides 500 secondary overflow seats.

Operational Variable Standard Specification Operational Rule
Total Bus Fleet 8 Vehicles (5 Coach, 3 Electric) Fixed fleet; no additional vehicles permitted
Vehicle Doors 1 Usable Door per Bus Controlled single-file ingress/egress
Hostel Release Time 06:00:00 (t=0) Simultaneous release across all dormitories
Staging Priority Tekun and Saujana First, Restu Last Restu holds at Restu cafe until cleared
Primary Venue Capacity DTSP: 3,000 Seats Main assembly hall
Secondary Overflow Dewan Budaya G03: 500 Seats Secondary authorized overflow facility

2. Operational Scope

This document outlines a candidate proposal pending simulation and field validation. It defines candidate route cycles, staff stations, and venue entry policies. Strict adherence ensures safe transit, reduced vehicle friction, and timely commencement of orientation ceremonies.

3. Current Baseline Bottlenecks

Historical orientation days created long queues and traffic delays. When all hostels surge onto roadways simultaneously, bus queues stall. Linear single-file holding causes severe crowding outside dormitories.

Figure 1: Baseline Bottleneck Model showing uncoordinated surge and single queue collapse.

Root Failure Points

The main error in prior years was treating all hostels equally at boarding points. Restu has a large headcount. When Restu students enter boarding areas first, smaller cohorts cannot access transit, creating system-wide starvation.

4. Target Optimized Flow Architecture

The revised architecture decouples arrival, holding, and boarding. Desasiswa Tekun and Saujana board immediately upon release. Restu holds at Restu cafe. This eliminates boarding starvation and stabilizes bus turnaround times.

Figure 2: Target Staged Architecture separating hostel staging from continuous vehicle loops.

System Improvements

This model prevents roadside queuing. Students remain seated in sheltered spaces. Continuous vehicle circulation reduces traffic congestion and boarding starvation.

5. Cohort Priority & Cafe Holding

Hostels differ significantly in resident count. Tekun and Saujana have lower populations and clear rapidly. Restu has a large headcount. Sequencing smaller hostels first clears loading zones quickly.

Figure 3: Hostel Dispatch Sequencing Timeline and Cafe Staging Protocol.

Restu Cafe Staging Protocol

Restu students assemble inside the sheltered Restu cafe at 06:00:00. PPSL marshals meter students toward the boarding bays only after Tekun and Saujana cohorts clear the pickup apron.

6. PPSL Staff Roles & Station Deployment

PPSL (Program Pembimbing Siswa Lestari) workers are event facilitators and headcount controllers (154 total PPSL staff across campus duties). They do not drive vehicles or conduct security screenings. They supervise orderly queues and verify headcounts.

8. Eight-Bus Continuous Loop Mechanics

The operational fleet consists of exactly 8 buses: 5 coach buses and 3 electric buses. Each vehicle has one usable door for student entry. The candidate proposal models continuous loop cycles between DUP staging and DTSP.

Figure 6: Continuous Loop Fleet Distribution (5 Coach and 3 EV units in synchronized transit).

Fleet Ingress & Capacity Physics

Planning models apply a conservative 180s full-coach boarding and 180s alighting dwell. Exact electric bus capacity remains unmeasured. Student headcounts occur at designated staff stations rather than at vehicle doors.

9. DTSP Drop-off Zone & Ingress Rules

The DTSP drop-off area is a wide straight road and car park capable of docking multiple buses concurrently. Although buses have only one usable door, multiple buses unload at the same time without creating vehicular bottlenecks.

Crucial Operational Rule: Zero door checks at DTSP entrance doors (no ticket or ID screening dwell). Students walk directly into the hall and take their seats. Pre-arrival headcount at hostel departure points eliminates double-screening.

Drop-Off Bay Management

Four dedicated docking bays operate simultaneously outside DTSP. Upon stopping, bus doors open immediately. Empty buses pull forward and begin the return loop to DUP without waiting for trailing vehicles.

Docking Bay Vehicle Type Target Disembark Time Discharge Route
Bay 1 (North) Coach (65–80 pax effective) Conservative ~180 s baseline Direct egress to Jalan Universiti
Bay 2 (Center-North) Coach (65–80 pax effective) Conservative ~180 s baseline Direct egress to Jalan Universiti
Bay 3 (Center-South) Electric (Capacity unmeasured) Conservative baseline pending trial Turnaround via Roundabout
Bay 4 (South) Electric (Capacity unmeasured) Conservative baseline pending trial Turnaround via Roundabout

Pedestrian Safety Measures

Physical barriers isolate bus movement lanes from disembarking passenger footpaths. PPSL ushers guide students immediately onto the covered concourse toward DTSP entrance portals.

10. Venue Capacities: DTSP & G03 Overflow

DTSP full-hall capacity is confirmed at ~3,000 seats. Dewan Budaya G03 serves as the official active secondary overflow venue, providing ~500 seats. Pre-DTSP wait occurs in a nearby lecture hall, never along Jalan Perpustakaan.

Figure 7: Venue Layout: DTSP Full Hall (3,000 seats), Pre-Wait Hall, and G03 Overflow (500 seats).

Overflow Trigger Protocol

Assignment of cohorts to DTSP versus Dewan Budaya G03 must be fixed pre-event from verified attendance and confirmed venue capacities, and changed only by the named command lead. Dewan Budaya G03 (~500 seats) serves as an active authorized destination.

12. Risk Management & Contingency Protocols

Operational resilience requires predetermined countermeasures for inclement weather, vehicle mechanical failure, and venue capacity overflows.

Risk Event Probability & Impact Prescribed Action Protocol
Heavy Tropical Rain High Prob • Med Impact Activate covered walkway pathways. Restu students remain sheltered in Restu cafe until buses dock at covered canopy.
Vehicle Breakdown (1 Bus) Med Prob • High Impact Remaining 7 buses accelerate loop cycle. Headway interval adjusts from 2.5 min to 3.0 min. Do not add external vehicles.
DTSP Full Capacity (3,000) High Prob • Med Impact Immediately divert remaining arriving buses to Dewan Budaya G03 (500 seats). Station Charlie PPSL activates video stream link.
Drop-Off Concourse Surge Med Prob • High Impact Direct disembarked students into the pre-wait lecture hall rather than holding on Jalan Perpustakaan road margins.

Communication Failsafe

If radio frequency interference occurs, PPSL leaders communicate via encrypted cellular mobile group channels with designated backup runners stationed at each terminal.
